quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious car crash?

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle off the road if possible. If someone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in damage (or more than $200 in damage to government property like signs).

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
About the same.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. It is harder to see in the dark. Headlights from other cars can blind you. There are more tired and impaired drivers on the road at night.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming cars may not see you pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid something in the road. Always be alert when driving near bicycles.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gas?

options.text: Leaving the car running in the driveway.
Speeding up quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: When you brake hard, you use fuel to speed up again. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking, you will use less gas.

questions.question: Where should your car be when you make a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the road.
Close to the left side of the road.
Close to the right side of the road.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move to the right side of the road. Do not cut across other lanes when making a turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What happens if a driver or passenger does not wear a safety belt?

options.text: Nothing.
A warning.
A fine for each person not wearing a safety belt.
Jail time.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fine for each person not wearing a safety belt.
questions.explanation: In Texas, drivers and passengers who do not wear safety belts can receive a fine. Children under 17 must be in a safety seat or safety belt. Anyone 15 or older can be cited for not wearing a safety belt. There are no exceptions to safety belt laws.

questions.question: How far before a turn should you signal?

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
20 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Use your turn signal or hand signal to tell other drivers what you plan to do. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: How close to a crosswalk can you park?

options.text: 20 feet
30 feet
35 feet
45 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk. Parking too close to a crosswalk can cause a crash.

questions.question: How far behind a motorcycle should you stop?

options.text: One full vehicle length.
Three full vehicle lengths.
Two feet.
Four feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: One full vehicle length.
questions.explanation: Stop one full vehicle length behind a motorcycle. This distance helps prevent a crash if another car hits you from behind. Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions, so stay alert.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel too much in the opposite direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer the wheel in the same direction the car is sliding.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Cars are going opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Cars are going opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
Cars are going the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Cars are going the same direction. You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars are going opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should drivers do when preparing to turn left?

options.text: Slow down gradually and check the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multi-lane road, move to the left lane before the intersection. Wait for traffic and pedestrians to clear, then turn.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: As long as you are not the driver.
If you sit in the back seat.
If you ride in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road or sidewalk. You cannot store open alcohol in the areas where the driver or passengers sit.

questions.question: A car is entering the freeway from an entrance ramp into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and position the same.
Honk to let them know you are there.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.
Change lanes or slow down to give them room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to give them room.
questions.explanation: Make space for vehicles entering the freeway. When you can, change lanes to let them merge smoothly and safely. If you cannot change lanes, slow down.

questions.question: Your vehicle is in an accident and is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle under any conditions.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Do not leave the scene without identifying yourself and offering help.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly in which conditions?

options.text: On flat roads.
On curvy roads.
In sunny areas.
In shaded areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: In shaded areas.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful in shaded areas created by trees or buildings. These spots freeze faster than other parts of the road and are the last to dry.

questions.question: When passing a car on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left soon.
Return to the right lane right away.
You can drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.

questions.question: How does a driver's emotional state affect their driving?

options.text: They drive the same as usual.
They can drive faster because their senses are sharper.
They should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
They should call someone to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Worry, anger, crying, and sadness make it harder to drive safely. Emotions distract your mind from the road. Take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must do. It means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake immediately. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the accelerator. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull safely off the road.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the movement shown by the arrow if they choose to.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers in that lane must always stop before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells drivers in that lane they must move in the direction shown by the arrow. Follow all traffic signs and signals before moving in that direction.

questions.question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street or highway, start from:

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a multilane one-way street or highway, always start from the left lane.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors often to spot tailgaters. If a car is following too closely, slow down gradually and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When can you park in the striped area next to a disabled parking spot?

options.text: Never.
When you have a disability plate or parking placard.
When all other parking spaces are full.
When you are parking for just a few minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot park in the striped areas next to disabled parking spaces. These spaces are needed for wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly and carefully where children are playing. Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road will make a sharp turn to the right and then a sharp turn to the left.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.
